parameters.query:
WITH handover AS (
  SELECT nullif($1::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS item
),
claim AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN h.item ->> 'run_id' ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
      THEN (h.item ->> 'run_id')::bigint
    END AS run_id
  FROM handover h
),
run AS (
  SELECT r.domain_id
  FROM runs r
  WHERE r.id = (SELECT run_id FROM claim)
)
-- The first node after the trigger, and the shape the parent design fixes for every
-- workflow in this set (.specs/2026-08-19-research-pipeline-port.md, section 4): the
-- domain's personas and taxonomy, read as ONE query answering exactly one row. Both
-- halves are argued in full on ar-ingest's Load Domain Context, which asks the same
-- question of the same tables and is not repeated here. What is written out below is
-- what differs, which is the run this canvas is handed and the projection it cuts.

-- THE RUN WAS OPENED FOR AN EXPORT SUBSCRIPTION. ar-dispatch claims two tables side
-- by side and this canvas is the second one's target: AR_EXPORT_WORKFLOW_ID pairs a
-- claimed export unit with this workflow the way AR_TOPIC_WORKFLOW_ID pairs a
-- claimed topic with ar-ingest. The row read here is the one that dispatcher opened
-- before invoking, and the domain comes off it rather than off any member of the
-- hand-over item, which is ar-ingest's shape: a domain named on the item as well
-- would be a second statement of something the run already carries, and two
-- statements of one fact can disagree with nothing reporting it.

-- WHICH SUBSCRIPTION IT WAS DOES NOT ARRIVE. Open Run in ar-dispatch returns the run
-- id alone, so the claimed unit does not survive the hop and this statement could
-- not read it if it wanted to. Naming that is the point rather than working around
-- it here: what a pass was dispatched for is a question about export_subscriptions
-- rows in this domain, and answering it belongs to the group that selects what a
-- digest covers rather than to the node that resolves the domain.

-- The whole hand-over item binds as ONE jsonb parameter rather than one parameter
-- per member, which is ar-research's Load Domain Context and is argued in full
-- there: JSON.stringify makes any item a valid jsonb literal, the nullif is what
-- keeps JSON.stringify(null) from arriving as a value, ->> answers NULL for every
-- jsonb that is not an object so a shape somebody else chose raises nothing, and the
-- {1,18} digit bound is what keeps a longer run of digits from overflowing the cast.

-- Three readings come out of this row and they are not two. A null run_id means the
-- item named no run this statement could read. A run_id with a null domain_id means
-- it named one that matches no runs row. A domain row means the pass resolved, and
-- an empty list beside it is a domain that states no personas, no categories, no
-- terms or no criteria. Read them in that order: a length says nothing until both
-- have been read.

-- Nothing here refuses. A digest pass with no domain has nothing to select and no
-- briefing to write, and a refusal at the top of this workflow would end it with the
-- runs row the dispatcher opened still waiting to be closed. What this answers
-- instead is a row saying what it could and could not resolve.

-- run_id travels as the parameter rather than as a column read back, so it survives
-- a run id that resolves to nothing. It has to travel because this node's answer
-- REPLACES the item the trigger was handed: whatever the dispatcher sent is gone
-- past here, and the run is what a ledger row, a stored briefing and the closing
-- update are all charged to. The invocation itself stays reachable at
-- $('Execute Workflow Trigger').first().json, which is the handle every node here
-- has on it.

-- Every list is ordered, which nothing downstream requires and every reader benefits
-- from: two passes over one unchanged domain hand the nodes below the same lists in
-- the same order, so a diff between two digests is about the findings rather than
-- about the order a planner happened to return rows in.
SELECT
  (SELECT run_id FROM claim) AS run_id,
  (SELECT domain_id FROM run) AS domain_id,
  -- The domain row, cut to the members a digest pass reads, and the same four
  -- ar-research fetches rather than the six ar-ingest and ar-score do. Those two
  -- carry feature_version and embedding_model because a feature vector is composed
  -- on those canvases, and nothing here composes one. What is left is read on both
  -- sides of the boundary this workflow stops at: slug and name are the identity an
  -- operator reads a pass by and the values a renderer under src/exports/ puts in a
  -- path and a title, and settings is where the heading vocabulary comes from,
  -- DomainSettings.findingsDisplayName being the one member digest-assemble.ts
  -- reads off it. NULL rather than an empty object when the item named no run this
  -- statement could resolve, which is the second of the three readings above.
  (SELECT jsonb_build_object(
     'id', d.id,
     'slug', d.slug,
     'name', d.name,
     'settings', d.settings)
     FROM domains d
    WHERE d.id = (SELECT domain_id FROM run)) AS domain,

  -- The personas. system_text is operator-owned prose and is the trusted half of
  -- what prompt-frame.ts composes around an untrusted chunk, and the whole list
  -- travels rather than the one row a step needs: which role a step is framed
  -- against is that step's to decide, and picking a row out of a list already here
  -- is a read rather than a second query per role. A persona is a row and is never
  -- written into a file, and no node below may put a finding's own text where one
  -- belongs.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', p.id,
       'role', p.role,
       'system_text', p.system_text)
       ORDER BY p.role, p.id)
       FROM personas p
      WHERE p.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM run)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS personas,

  -- The categories, and on this canvas they are more than the buckets the terms
  -- below are filed under: they are the sections a digest is assembled into.
  -- digest-assemble.ts sections by the domain's own category keys, in the order
  -- they arrive, with one section for the findings under none, so this ORDER BY is
  -- what fixes the shape of a stored briefing. key rather than id is what the code
  -- matches on, and name is what a section is headed with when it is not the key.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', c.id,
       'key', c.key,
       'name', c.name,
       'parent_id', c.parent_id)
       ORDER BY c.key, c.id)
       FROM categories c
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM run)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS categories,

  -- The terms, joined to their category's key rather than carrying category_id, in
  -- the four-member spelling the rest of this set fetches them in. Nothing in a
  -- digest reads them: a period's prose is drafted from findings that were scored
  -- long before this pass, and re-reading the patterns behind those scores here
  -- would be a second opinion about work already recorded. They are selected
  -- because the design fixes the taxonomy as what this node fetches, and a term
  -- list selected in some other spelling would be one a node group added below
  -- could not hand to the libraries that read it.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'category', c.key,
       'pattern', t.pattern,
       'weight', t.weight,
       'polarity', t.polarity)
       ORDER BY c.key, t.pattern, t.id)
       FROM terms t
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = t.category_id
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM run)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS terms,

  -- The criteria, joined to their category the same way and here for the same
  -- reason. Nothing in a digest scores anything: criteria are ar-score's subject,
  -- and what a digest says about a finding is what the score already stored says.
  -- They complete the taxonomy this node is fixed to fetch, so a node group added
  -- below reads them without a second lookup and without a second branch to reason
  -- about.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', k.id,
       'category', c.key,
       'value', k.value,
       'kind', k.kind)
       ORDER BY c.key, k.kind, k.id)
       FROM criteria k
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = k.category_id
      WHERE k.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM run)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS criteria

WITH
-- What one digest covers, in one statement. The node above resolved the domain; this
-- one answers the material a pass is made of: which deliveries the domain has
-- standing, which findings fall inside the period this digest is for, and what the
-- pass before this one failed at. Every group below reads its input from here.

-- ONE ROW OUT, whatever the domain holds. Every member below is a scalar subquery and
-- the outer SELECT names no FROM, so this node answers exactly one item however many
-- findings or subscriptions there are to put in it. The groups below need it that
-- way: digest-assemble.ts takes a LIST of findings and answers one assembly, so a
-- digest is one item's work rather than one item per finding, and the briefings row a
-- pass writes is one row rather than one per finding selected.

-- WHICH SUBSCRIPTION THE TICK CLAIMED DOES NOT ARRIVE, and nothing here reconstructs
-- it. Open Run in ar-dispatch ends RETURNING id AS run_id and Invoke Target Workflow
-- hands the child the item on its input, so the claimed row's id is gone before this
-- workflow starts, which the trigger sticky states from the other side. What this
-- reads instead is every enabled export_subscriptions row the domain has, which is
-- the set that claim was taken from. A domain holding exactly one, which is the
-- ordinary shape, is answered exactly and subscription below IS that row. A domain
-- holding several is answered with all of them and a NULL where the one row would go,
-- because choosing among them would be this statement inventing a fact about the
-- pass.

-- That costs the pass nothing, which is why the missing member is worth naming rather
-- than working around. What a digest pass PRODUCES does not depend on which
-- subscription it was dispatched for: briefings in src/db/schema/runs.ts argues that
-- storing the digest is what makes every format render the SAME text, so the row this
-- pass writes is the same row whichever enabled subscription came due. A format
-- selects a renderer and nothing else, and running one is the service layer's work in
-- a later phase. Where the exact row is wanted, the repair is a wider RETURNING in
-- ar-dispatch and a member read here, the two together.

-- THE WINDOW IS BOUNDED BY WHAT WAS LAST STORED AND NOT BY A CLOCK. briefings carries
-- no column naming the period a row covers, which that table records as the trade it
-- makes, so the boundary available here is the generated_at stamp on the newest
-- stored row. A domain with a briefing already stored gets the findings created since
-- that stamp. A domain with none gets its whole corpus, once, and every pass after it
-- gets one period. Nothing here reads now(), so two passes an hour apart over an
-- unchanged domain select the same findings.

-- The bound is inclusive, and that is the direction that carries rather than loses. A
-- finding created at exactly the stamp could only have been in the previous digest if
-- that pass had selected a row written at its own write moment, which it could not:
-- the selection is an earlier node than the write. So the tie duplicates nothing and
-- an exclusive bound would drop it.

-- What no bound of this shape can cover is said rather than implied. A pass selects
-- at one moment and its briefing is stamped at a later one, so a finding written
-- between the two is outside this digest and outside the next one, whose window
-- starts at that stamp. Closing it needs the selection's own high water mark stored
-- on the briefing, which is a column that table does not have.

-- NO LIMIT ON THE FINDINGS, and its absence is a decision rather than an omission. A
-- row cap here would make the window lie: what it dropped would never come round
-- again, the next pass starting from this briefing's stamp, so a capped first pass
-- over a long corpus would lose its tail silently and permanently. The unbounded pass
-- is the first one over a domain that has never had a digest, and it happens once.
-- What the model group below may SPEND is declared there, over what it drafts, which
-- bounds a cost rather than what the period covered.

-- TWO PARAMETERS, in declaration order: the run and the domain. Both are read off the
-- context item above rather than out of the hand over a second time. That node has
-- already resolved the domain off the run, and deriving it a second way here is how
-- the two start being able to disagree. A NULL domain selects nothing and reaches an
-- empty list on every member, which is where a pass started by hand ends.
stored AS (
  -- The stamp the window is bounded by, as a CTE that always answers one row. The
  -- inner query answers the newest stored briefing for this domain and NULL where the
  -- domain has none, so a cross join below reads the boundary without a second lookup
  -- and without a branch: since IS NULL is the whole test for a domain that has never
  -- had a digest.

  -- generated_at then id, because the stamp does not order these rows on its own.
  -- now() is the transaction's start time, so two briefings written together tie to
  -- the microsecond, which briefings.generated_at names as the reason a reader
  -- wanting the current one says ORDER BY generated_at DESC LIMIT 1 rather than
  -- assuming one row per period. id breaks the tie, the later insert winning.
  SELECT (SELECT b.generated_at
            FROM briefings b
           WHERE b.domain_id = $2::bigint
           ORDER BY b.generated_at DESC, b.id DESC
           LIMIT 1) AS since
),

subscribed AS (
  -- The deliveries this domain has standing: every enabled export_subscriptions row
  -- it holds. The header above says why this is a set rather than the one claimed row
  -- and what that costs.

  -- ENABLED and not every row, because a disabled subscription is configuration
  -- somebody kept rather than a delivery: export_subscriptions.enabled records that
  -- disabling is not cancelling, cancelling being a DELETE. The dispatcher's own
  -- claim filters the same way, so this set and the set the claim was taken from are
  -- the same rows.
  SELECT s.id, s.format, s.connector_id
  FROM export_subscriptions s
  WHERE s.domain_id = $2::bigint
    AND s.enabled
),

covered AS (
  -- The findings this digest covers: the domain's own, created at or after the
  -- boundary above. The cross join is what makes since readable on every row, the CTE
  -- answering exactly one, and it can drop nothing.

  -- domain_id is the predicate rather than a join through documents or sources,
  -- because findings.domain_id is NOT NULL and says which domain a finding belongs to
  -- directly. A finding of another domain is not this domain's period whatever it was
  -- read out of.
  SELECT f.id, f.domain_id, f.document_id, f.entity_id, f.fields,
         f.score, f.score_version, f.created_at
  FROM findings f
  CROSS JOIN stored w
  WHERE f.domain_id = $2::bigint
    AND (w.since IS NULL OR f.created_at >= w.since)
),

closed AS (
  -- The run before this one, and its failures. previousRunBanner in
  -- digest-assemble.ts carries this value into a banner entry rather than dropping
  -- it, so a period whose pass before it failed says so in the digest instead of only
  -- in a table nobody reading a digest opens.

  -- CLOSED means finished_at is set, which is a reading rather than a definition runs
  -- makes: src/db/schema/runs.ts records that a row saying failed with no finish, and
  -- one carrying a finish while still saying running, are both storable and that only
  -- the writer pairs them. finished_at is the one of the two that also orders, so it
  -- is what this reads and what it orders by, id breaking a tie between two runs
  -- closed in one transaction.

  -- The run this pass is charged to is excluded BY NAME and not only by being open.
  -- IS DISTINCT FROM answers true for a NULL parameter, so a pass started by hand
  -- still reads a previous run, and a pass re-invoked against a run somebody already
  -- closed does not read its own errors back as the ones before it.

  -- WHICHEVER WORKFLOW OPENED IT. runs carries no column naming its writer, which
  -- Open Run in ar-dispatch states at length, so the newest closed row for this
  -- domain is an ingest, a capture, a score, a research or an export pass and this
  -- statement cannot tell them apart. That is the right reading anyway: what a digest
  -- reports is that the domain's last pass failed at something, not which canvas it
  -- was.
  SELECT r.errors
  FROM runs r
  WHERE r.domain_id = $2::bigint
    AND r.finished_at IS NOT NULL
    AND r.id IS DISTINCT FROM $1::bigint
  ORDER BY r.finished_at DESC, r.id DESC
  LIMIT 1
)

SELECT
  $1::bigint AS run_id,
  $2::bigint AS domain_id,

  -- The boundary itself, carried so the groups below can say what period this digest
  -- is for. It is the only member that can: briefings has no period column, so a
  -- stored row's coverage is this stamp and the one on the row before it.
  (SELECT w.since FROM stored w) AS since,

  -- The subscription this pass was dispatched for, when that is answerable, and NULL
  -- when it is not. Exactly one enabled row makes it that row; none and several both
  -- make it NULL, which the list below tells apart. A CASE with no ELSE is what
  -- writes the NULL, and the reasoning is in the header.
  CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM subscribed) = 1
       THEN (SELECT jsonb_build_object(
               'id', s.id,
               'format', s.format,
               'connector_id', s.connector_id)
               FROM subscribed s)
  END AS subscription,

  -- Every enabled subscription, in the order the row's own natural key gives:
  -- export_subscriptions is UNIQUE over domain, format and connector, so format then
  -- connector_id is a total order over one domain's rows and id is there for a reader
  -- rather than to break a tie. Three members each, and they are the three the
  -- natural key is made of: id is what addresses the row, format is what selects a
  -- renderer, and connector_id is what tells two subscriptions of one format apart.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', s.id,
       'format', s.format,
       'connector_id', s.connector_id)
       ORDER BY s.format, s.connector_id, s.id)
       FROM subscribed s),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS subscriptions,

  -- The findings, ordered by score with absence last, then by the creation stamp,
  -- then by the id. compareFindings in src/lib/digest-assemble.ts is the same
  -- ordering as TypeScript and says why each key points the way it does; the two are
  -- written down twice because the rows are ordered here before that module ever sees
  -- them and a renderer lays out the order it was handed.

  -- NULLS LAST is load bearing rather than tidy. DESC orders nulls FIRST in Postgres
  -- by default, so without it every unscored finding would head the digest, which is
  -- the opposite of what an unscored finding means: findings.score records that a
  -- score nothing measured is absent rather than zero, and compareScores sorts
  -- absence behind every score there is rather than below the lowest one.

  -- created_at needs no NULLS clause, the column being NOT NULL. The library reads
  -- absence there anyway, because a value crossing a JSON boundary may arrive as
  -- something no reading can make a moment of, which is a claim about the transport
  -- rather than about the column.

  -- Eight members, and they are the eight ExportFindingRow in src/exports/index.ts
  -- names. What the assembly sections and what a renderer is later handed are then
  -- one shape rather than two that can drift. Two of them are read by nothing on this
  -- canvas: document_id and entity_id are provenance for a person following a finding
  -- back to the material it came out of, and the stored payload is the only place a
  -- digest keeps it.

  -- A score arrives as a JSON number here rather than as the string a numeric column
  -- answers with at the top level of a Postgres node's row, jsonb rendering it as a
  -- number. Both are read, which toScore in digest-assemble.ts states, so neither
  -- spelling is anything a group below has to know about.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', c.id,
       'domain_id', c.domain_id,
       'document_id', c.document_id,
       'entity_id', c.entity_id,
       'fields', c.fields,
       'score', c.score,
       'score_version', c.score_version,
       'created_at', c.created_at)
       ORDER BY c.score DESC NULLS LAST, c.created_at DESC, c.id DESC)
       FROM covered c),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS findings,

  -- The previous run's failures, whole, in the shape the column holds them. NULL here
  -- is no previous closed run at all, where an empty array is a run that closed
  -- having failed at nothing, and previousRunBanner answers no banner for both.
  (SELECT r.errors FROM closed r) AS previous_errors

WITH
-- Where the address of the model this pass calls is read, and the only node in this
-- group that can read one. A Code node opens no connection and a spliced library
-- imports nothing, so the endpoint and the model name arrive here as data or the
-- nodes below have nothing to call. ar-ingest carries a node of this name asking the
-- same question of the same table and argues the whole of it, including why the
-- oldest llm row wins and why neither member is validated anywhere before this
-- projection. What is written out here is the half that differs.

-- ONE READ FOR THE PASS, on that node's reasoning. executeOnce runs this against the
-- first item it was handed and answers once, and which service this deployment calls
-- is a fact about the deployment rather than about any one period.

-- THE FIRST ITEM IS THE ASSEMBLED DIGEST, AND IT IS THE ONLY ITEM. That is what
-- parts this node from both siblings, where the first item is one of a batch and
-- which one arrived first is a property of an ordering. Assemble Digest answers
-- exactly one item by construction, briefings taking one row per pass, so there is no
-- question here about which item executeOnce read.

-- EVERY PASS REACHES THIS NODE, which is the other difference and the larger one. At
-- ingest and at research a pass with an empty queue never gets here at all, so the
-- table is read only when there was something to spend on. Here the node above
-- answers its one item whatever the period held, so this statement runs on a pass
-- that resolved no domain and on a period that came to nothing alike, and what
-- decides whether anything is spent is the node below rather than the arrival of an
-- item.

-- One parameter, the run, read off the item this node was handed. It travels for the
-- reason it travels everywhere on this canvas: the ledger row below is charged to the
-- run and not to a period.
connector AS (
  -- The llm connector, by kind, oldest first and capped at one. connectors is not
  -- domain scoped and nothing on a domain row names one, so there is nothing here to
  -- narrow by. The sibling states what the cap decides and what reconfiguring rather
  -- than adding a rival buys.
  SELECT c.id, c.name, c.config
  FROM connectors c
  WHERE c.kind = 'llm'
  ORDER BY c.id
  LIMIT 1
)

SELECT
-- Two members read out of the config object, each read as text only where it IS text
-- and with the empty string taken for an absence. connectors.config carries no type
-- annotation, its shape being the client's business, so nothing has validated either
-- of these and this projection is where they are first read.

-- A null endpoint means there is nowhere to reach, and the node below refuses on it
-- by name rather than passing it on. The subscription's own connector_id is NOT what
-- is read here and is not a rival reading of the same fact: that row names where a
-- rendered artifact is delivered to, which is a question for a later phase and for
-- something outside this canvas, where this names where the prose is drafted.

-- A null model is an ordinary state and not a refusal. A gateway that routes, or a
-- runtime serving whatever it was started with, takes no model name, and
-- llm_calls.model is nullable for exactly that.

-- connector_id and connector_name are carried for a reader rather than for a caller.
-- Nothing below binds either one. They travel because the node that made a call and
-- the row that named the service should be readable together on the canvas.
  $1::bigint AS run_id,
  (SELECT c.id FROM connector c) AS connector_id,
  (SELECT c.name FROM connector c) AS connector_name,
  (SELECT nullif(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(c.config -> 'endpoint') = 'string'
                      THEN c.config ->> 'endpoint'
                 END, '')
     FROM connector c) AS endpoint,
  (SELECT nullif(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(c.config -> 'model') = 'string'
                      THEN c.config ->> 'model'
                 END, '')
     FROM connector c) AS model

WITH
-- Where a call is accounted for. One row per call, charged to the run that made it,
-- and src/db/schema/runs.ts argues at length what that buys: the runs row accounts
-- for a pass as a whole, and these rows account for the same work one call at a time,
-- which is the granularity the question of what a call cost is asked at. ar-ingest
-- carries a node of this name writing the same table, and the attribution argument,
-- the no-conflict-target argument and the position-pairing argument are all made
-- there rather than repeated here.

-- THE CEILING AND THIS ROW ARE ONE PROPERTY read from two ends. Apply Call Ceiling
-- states what a pass WILL spend and these rows are what it did, so a ceiling that
-- quietly stopped being applied reads exactly like a pass whose period happened to be
-- quiet. Neither half is enforced by anything in this schema, which is why the
-- property is asserted over the built artifact instead.

-- ONE ROW OUT PER CALL. The insert sits in a CTE and the outer SELECT names no FROM,
-- so this node answers exactly one item for every item it was handed, and the group
-- below stores a briefing whether or not the call came back with anything. An
-- INSERT ... RETURNING on its own would emit nothing for a statement that wrote no
-- row, and a digest pass whose drafting failed still has a period to store.

-- THE PAIRING IS ONE POSITION HERE, which is what parts this from both siblings. They
-- bound a plural batch and pair a call against the item it was made from by position;
-- this canvas bounds its batch at one drafting call per pass, so the position bound
-- below is zero on every pass that reaches this node. The shape is written the same
-- way regardless, because what makes the pairing correct is the node above answering
-- one item per item it ran on, and that is a property of that node rather than of the
-- number of items it happened to have.

-- WHAT BEING WRONG ABOUT IT WOULD COST is correspondingly smaller than at research,
-- where a swap would file one candidate's answer under another's subject. Here there
-- is nothing to swap with. What the reading is still load bearing for is the run: the
-- measurements below come off the prepared item, so an item that was not the one this
-- call was made from would charge a real call the wrong prompt size.

-- THREE PARAMETERS, in declaration order: the run, the model name, and the prepared
-- item this call was made from. The first two are read off Select Model Connector,
-- which answered one row for the whole pass, so neither is a per call reading and
-- neither needs pairing.

-- BOUND AS ONE JSONB VALUE rather than as a member per column: fewer values for the
-- comma splitter to get wrong, and the members are read out here where a comment can
-- say what each one is.
prepared AS (
  SELECT $3::jsonb AS item
),

-- What the row says about the call, cast once. prompt_chars and est_tokens are in the
-- signal class the schema calls out: null means nothing measured this call, and zero
-- is a real reading rather than a stand in for one. Neither is COALESCEd to zero.

-- The node name is a literal and is known by construction: the step that made the
-- call is the node above this one, and its own name is the one fact it cannot fail to
-- have. It is Draft Digest Prose rather than the endpoint hanging off it, because the
-- endpoint is where the credential sits and the chain node is what a pass asked.

-- The model is nullable and arrives so. A gateway that routes, or a runtime serving
-- whatever it was started with, takes no model name, and what is stored is what was
-- asked for rather than what served it.
call AS (
  SELECT
    nullif($2::text, '') AS model,
    (p.item ->> 'prompt_chars')::integer AS prompt_chars,
    (p.item ->> 'est_tokens')::integer AS est_tokens
  FROM prepared p
),

written AS (
  INSERT INTO llm_calls (run_id, node, model, prompt_chars, est_tokens)
  SELECT
    $1::bigint,
    'Draft Digest Prose',
    c.model,
    c.prompt_chars,
    c.est_tokens
  FROM call c
  RETURNING id
)

SELECT
-- The item this node answers, and it is about the period rather than about the call.
-- The run and the domain come back out of the prepared item, which is what the
-- briefing row and the closing update are both charged to. Both were derived above
-- this node, and passing them through here is a carry rather than a second
-- derivation.

-- The drafted prose is deliberately not among them: it is a model's own text, it is
-- reachable off Draft Digest Prose by name, and routing it through a SQL parameter to
-- get here would be a round trip that changes nothing about it. The assembled payload
-- is absent for the same reason and one better -- it never entered the prompt either,
-- so it has stayed exactly where Assemble Digest decided it.

-- llm_call_id is the ledger row this call left behind. Nothing below reads it today.
-- It travels because the row and the item it was written for are otherwise joined by
-- nothing at all, this table carrying no reference to a briefing or a period.
  $1::bigint AS run_id,
  (SELECT (p.item ->> 'domain_id')::bigint FROM prepared p) AS domain_id,
  (SELECT w.id FROM written w) AS llm_call_id

parameters.query:
WITH
-- Where the digest a pass came to is stored, and the whole of what this canvas
-- produces about the period. briefings in src/db/schema/runs.ts is the account a
-- PERSON reads: what a period came to under one domain's taxonomy, written once and
-- kept, rather than assembled again by whichever surface happens to ask.

-- STORING IT IS WHAT MAKES EVERY FORMAT RENDER THE SAME TEXT. That table argues it
-- and src/exports/index.ts argues it again from the renderer side: an export and the
-- API serve one artifact rather than two renderings able to disagree about what a
-- period came to. A renderer handed the findings and asked to compose prose out of
-- them would be exactly that second rendering, and there would be no answer to which
-- of the two a domain had said. So the row is written once, here, and every renderer
-- reads it back.

-- THIS IS WHERE THE SEND-FREE RULE LEAVES A DIGEST PASS ABLE TO FINISH.
-- docs/architecture/00-overview.md states the rule: the workflows write to the
-- database, renderers return artifacts, and an email export produces a draft and
-- stops there. A pass that drafted a digest and could neither store nor deliver it
-- would have spent a model call for nothing, so what it produces has to land
-- somewhere that is not a delivery, and a row is that somewhere. Everything above
-- this node is selection, assembly and one call; this is the node that makes a pass
-- worth having run.

-- NO ARTIFACT IS WRITTEN ANYWHERE BY THIS CANVAS. Nothing here opens a file, reaches
-- a vault, addresses a recipient or resolves a destination, and the subscription rows
-- Select Digest Material read name a FORMAT rather than a place this statement writes
-- to. Rendering is a module under src/exports/, outside this workflow, held to a
-- transport-free rule of its own by tests/invariants/exports-send-free.test.ts, and
-- what it renders is the row written here.

-- A NULL BODY IS NOT AN EMPTY ONE, and the two are parted below rather than
-- COALESCEd together. NULL means no text was produced, which is a drafting call that
-- came back with nothing or one that failed; '' would claim a briefing was written
-- and that it came to nothing, which a surface then renders as a blank document
-- rather than as nothing to show. The body column states the split and
-- src/exports/markdown-body.ts is what acts on it.

-- THE PROSE IS STORED AS THE MODEL WROTE IT. Nothing here reduces it, and that is
-- deliberate rather than an omission: a Postgres node splices no library, and every
-- renderer puts the stored body through sanitizeUntrusted on its own way out. The
-- assembled half beside it was reduced before it was assembled, Assemble Digest
-- having done it to text that came out of this domain's own tables. Neither is
-- bounded here, briefings.body being unbounded for the reason that column gives.

-- ONE ROW PER PASS AND NO CONFLICT TARGET. briefings has a surrogate key and no
-- unique constraint over a period, so a second render inserts a rival row rather than
-- meeting the first, and the current digest is ORDER BY generated_at DESC LIMIT 1.
-- That is the accumulate-versus-replace trade the table argues, and it is the same
-- stamp Select Digest Material bounds a window with, so the row written here is where
-- the next pass over this domain starts its period.

-- A PASS THAT STAGED NOTHING DOES NOT REACH THIS NODE, which is the open half of that
-- ending rather than something this statement can answer. Apply Call Ceiling stages
-- nothing for a period that came to nothing and nothing for a pass that resolved no
-- domain, so the chain ends there and neither writes a briefing. A row saying a
-- period came to nothing is exactly what a reader of a quiet domain wants, and
-- reaching it needs a wire this group does not have: that node cannot emit an item
-- nobody could draft from, buildChunk refusing an empty body, so the repair is a path
-- around the model group rather than a flag on it. Its own header hands the question
-- here and names the mechanism this canvas already uses for the shape, ar-ingest's
-- Score Findings.

-- FOUR PARAMETERS, in declaration order: the run, the domain, the drafting answer and
-- the assembled item. The first two are read off the item this node was handed and
-- are not re-derived, which is the rule every node on this canvas follows. The other
-- two are bound whole, as JSONB, for the reason Ledger Model Call gives -- fewer
-- values for the comma splitter to get wrong, and the members read out here where a
-- comment can say what each one is.

-- domain_id IS NOT NULL ON THAT TABLE AND IS NOT DEFENDED HERE. A pass reaches this
-- node only through Apply Call Ceiling, which stages nothing unless the assembly
-- counted findings, and a pass that resolved no domain counted none. A null arriving
-- is a canvas contradicting itself rather than an absence to handle, and the column
-- reports it loudly, which is the right volume for a state that cannot happen.
handed AS (
  SELECT
    $3::jsonb AS drafted,
    $4::jsonb AS assembled
),

-- The two halves of the briefing, read out of what the nodes above answered.

-- body is the drafted prose where the drafting step produced any, and SQL NULL
-- otherwise, the CASE carrying no ELSE. Three states arrive as nothing: an answer
-- with no text member at all, which is what Draft Digest Prose emits when its own
-- call failed and onError continueRegularOutput let the pass go on; a member that is
-- not a string; and text whose whole content is blank. The trim belongs to the
-- emptiness TEST alone -- what is stored is the untrimmed answer whenever anything
-- survives it, a model's own leading blank line being its text rather than a fault.

-- payload is the assembly Assemble Digest fixed, taken whole and uncounted. Every
-- number in it is that node's own reading and nothing here recomputes one, which is
-- what keeps the sections, the counts and the order one authority rather than two.
-- jsonb_typeof parts an object from the absences: a missing member and a JSON null
-- both answer something other than object and both take the column's {} default, a
-- briefing that recorded nothing structured and one whose writer keeps no structure
-- reading the same to every renderer.
briefing AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(h.drafted -> 'text') = 'string'
              AND btrim(h.drafted ->> 'text') <> ''
         THEN h.drafted ->> 'text'
    END AS body,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(h.assembled -> 'briefing_payload') = 'object'
         THEN h.assembled -> 'briefing_payload'
         ELSE '{}'::jsonb
    END AS payload
  FROM handed h
),

-- The write. Four columns named and two left to their defaults: payload has a {}
-- default this statement never reaches, the CASE above answering an object either
-- way, and generated_at dates the WRITE rather than the moment the period was
-- selected, which the column records as the limit it accepts. A pass that selected at
-- one time and persisted later would have to carry the first to record it, and
-- nothing on this canvas does.
written AS (
  INSERT INTO briefings (domain_id, run_id, body, payload)
  SELECT $2::bigint, $1::bigint, b.body, b.payload
  FROM briefing b
  RETURNING id, generated_at
)

SELECT
-- The item this node answers, and it is about the row rather than about the call
-- above it. The run and the domain travel because the group below closes the runs row
-- the dispatcher opened and is charged to both.

-- briefing_id is the row this statement left behind and generated_at is the stamp on
-- it, which is the boundary the NEXT pass over this domain selects from. Both come
-- out of the write rather than being read back off the table, so a statement that
-- wrote nothing answers null for them instead of answering a row some other pass
-- stored.

-- body_stored reports which of the two states the drafting step reached, and it is a
-- reading of the predicate the write was made under rather than a second look at the
-- column. The prose itself is deliberately not among the members: it is in the row
-- now, it is reachable off Draft Digest Prose by name for anything that wants it
-- before then, and carrying it forward would be a second copy of a value the group
-- below has no use for.
  $1::bigint AS run_id,
  $2::bigint AS domain_id,
  (SELECT w.id FROM written w) AS briefing_id,
  (SELECT w.generated_at FROM written w) AS generated_at,
  (SELECT b.body IS NOT NULL FROM briefing b) AS body_stored

WITH
-- Where a digest pass says what it did, and where the row the dispatcher opened stops
-- being open. runs in src/db/schema/runs.ts keeps that account in three columns
-- because a reader wanting any one of them should not have to parse the other two:
-- status is what the pass came to, counts is what it did, and errors is what it could
-- not do. This statement writes all three and the finish beside them.

-- THIS WORKFLOW CLOSES A ROW IT DID NOT OPEN, which is ar-ingest's shape rather than
-- ar-score's. ar-dispatch claimed an export subscription, opened a runs row against
-- this domain, and invoked this workflow with that row's id as the whole hand-over,
-- so the row already exists and this statement UPDATEs it. ar-score and ar-capture
-- INSERT one already closed instead, neither of them being dispatched. What follows
-- from the difference is the overlap below: this row has two writers.

-- THE DISPATCHER WRITES IT AGAIN AFTER THIS NODE DOES, and waits in order to. Invoke
-- Target Workflow sets waitForSubWorkflow, so ar-dispatch's Close Run Succeeded fires
-- on this node's answer and sets status and finished_at itself, landing an ok on top
-- of whatever is written here. That node names the open choice, between reading
-- errors on its side and holding every target to reporting its own status. What
-- survives either way is counts, which no statement in ar-dispatch touches, and
-- errors, which both sides APPEND to rather than assign. So the status written here
-- is the pass's own reading of itself, and the row's last word on it belongs to
-- whichever writer wrote last.

-- ANSWERING EXACTLY ONE ITEM IS WHAT KEEPS THAT SECOND WRITE SINGULAR. Close Run
-- Succeeded runs once per item this workflow returns, so a canvas answering three
-- would close the dispatcher's row three times. executeOnce is set here and the node
-- above already answers one item, which makes it a backstop and not the mechanism.

-- THE FORMAT IS RECORDED AS A COUNT AND NOT AS A VALUE. counts is annotated
-- Record<string, number>, and ar-score's own closing node refused to put a feature
-- version in it for exactly that reason, so which subscription this pass served is
-- written as a KEY instead: served_<format> at 1. A reader of the row can then say
-- which renderer the stored digest was dispatched for without joining anything, and
-- every value in the column is still a count. The key is built by concatenation, and
-- export_subscriptions_format_check already bounds that member to five spellings; the
-- pattern test below is what keeps a key from being built out of anything else that
-- reaches it.

-- WHICH SUBSCRIPTION IT WAS IS ANSWERABLE ONLY WHERE ONE IS ENABLED. Open Run in
-- ar-dispatch returns the run id alone, so the claimed row does not survive the hop,
-- and Select Digest Material answers a fail-closed identity in its place: the
-- subscription member is the row where the domain has exactly one enabled
-- subscription and NULL where it has none or several. No format key is written for
-- either of those, and subscriptions_enabled beside it is what says which of the two
-- happened. The repair is a wider RETURNING in ar-dispatch plus a member read here,
-- one change rather than two halves either side could make alone.

-- AN UNANSWERABLE SUBSCRIPTION IS NOT A FAILURE. A domain wanting one digest in two
-- formats is ordinary, and briefings in src/db/schema/runs.ts argues why it costs
-- nothing: a pass writes the SAME row whichever subscription came due, the format
-- selecting a renderer rather than changing what a period came to. So it is counted
-- and it moves no status.

-- AN UNMEASURED COUNT IS ABSENT RATHER THAN ZERO. This column cannot hold a null,
-- every value in it being a count, so the null-vs-zero rule this pipeline holds to
-- for a numeric signal is kept here by leaving the key out: jsonb_strip_nulls below
-- drops a member whose reading was not a number, and a reader then finds no key
-- rather than a zero claiming a quantity was measured at nought. The assembly's own
-- total is the one reading that can go absent, and it is a number on every pass that
-- reaches this node at all.

-- WHAT MAKES A PASS partial is a briefing stored with no prose in it, which is
-- fail-flag-keep read onto a digest: the structure Assemble Digest fixed is in the
-- row and the drafting call came back with nothing, and either neighbour loses half
-- of that. RUN_STATUSES in src/db/schema/values.ts argues the member at length.
-- failed is the narrower case where no row was written at all, which no path on this
-- canvas reaches, Store Briefing's insert being unconditional and a statement that
-- raised having failed that node instead of reaching this one. It is read fail-closed
-- anyway: a briefing id that did not arrive is a canvas contradicting itself rather
-- than an absence to smooth over.

-- WHAT DOES NOT REACH THIS NODE is the same limit the group above records. Every node
-- here is on one main chain and a node handed no item does not run, so a period that
-- came to nothing stops at Apply Call Ceiling and leaves the dispatcher's row at the
-- running default, which ar-dispatch cannot finish either, its success branch having
-- no item to fire on. The repair is a path around the model group, and it belongs to
-- the canvas topology rather than to this group.

-- THE TALLIES ARE COUNTED HERE AND GATHERED THERE. The parameter below carries one
-- list per node that can answer several items and one member per fact that is one per
-- pass, each cut to what a tally reads, and every rule about what those members MEAN
-- is in this statement. An expression can import nothing and is read by no gate in
-- this repository, so a rule written there would be a second copy of something with
-- nowhere to be compared. The projection is not cosmetic either: the selection's
-- findings carry whole field maps and the assembly carries the whole digest, and
-- binding either unprojected would ship the period's own corpus back to the database
-- to be counted.

-- AN ID IS TESTED AS TEXT AND NEVER BY TYPE. A bigint read as a top-level column
-- comes back off the driver as a STRING, so a ledger id arrives spelled "41" while an
-- id parsed out of a jsonb array arrives as the number 41. A tally written on
-- jsonb_typeof would count one spelling and miss the other, which is a count wrong by
-- a plausible amount rather than one that fails. Every id predicate below reads the
-- member's TEXT, which is the same either way and is NULL for an absent member and
-- for a JSON null.

-- NOTHING HERE CAN RAISE, which matters more at this node than anywhere else on the
-- canvas: a statement that threw would leave the run open with everything it is
-- reporting on already done. So the gathered object is guarded before it is read,
-- jsonb_each and jsonb_array_elements are handed a CASE rather than a member somebody
-- else built, and every cast sits behind a pattern test.

-- TWO PARAMETERS, in declaration order: the run and the gathered pass. The run is
-- read off Load Domain Context by name rather than off the item, which is where it
-- survives a domain that resolved to nothing. There is no third: this workflow
-- invokes nothing, so there is no sub-workflow error to carry the way both of
-- ar-ingest's invocations are carried into its own closing statement.
gathered AS (
  SELECT
    $1::bigint AS run_id,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof($2::jsonb) = 'object'
         THEN $2::jsonb
         ELSE '{}'::jsonb
    END AS pass
),

-- The lists the gathered pass carries, one row per item with the node it came from
-- beside it. jsonb_each raises on a value that is not an object and
-- jsonb_array_elements on one that is not an array, so both are guarded rather than
-- trusted. The members read as facts below are not arrays and contribute nothing
-- here, which is what lets one gathered object carry both shapes; a list that arrived
-- as something else contributes nothing for the same reason, leaving its tally at
-- nought instead of raising.
reading AS (
  SELECT e.key AS node, x.item AS item
  FROM gathered g,
       jsonb_each(g.pass) e,
       jsonb_array_elements(
         CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(e.value) = 'array'
              THEN e.value
              ELSE '[]'::jsonb
         END) AS x(item)
),

-- The facts that are one per pass rather than one per item, read as members. Every
-- node on this canvas answers exactly one item, so these are most of what there is to
-- read: a list of one element repeated per pass would be machinery answering a
-- question that has one answer.

-- subscription is the fail-closed identity Select Digest Material answered, taken
-- whole because its three members are the natural key export_subscriptions is unique
-- over and a reader following the count back wants the id and the connector as well
-- as the format.

-- findings_digested is the assembly's own total and is not recomputed here. Assemble
-- Digest counted it against the sections it read, and counting the stored payload
-- again would be a second authority on what the period came to. The pattern test is
-- what keeps a member that is not a whole number out of a column of counts.

-- briefing_id and body_stored are the two things the write below reports on, read off
-- what Store Briefing answered rather than by looking at the row again.
scope AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(g.pass -> 'subscription') = 'object'
         THEN g.pass -> 'subscription'
    END AS subscription,
    CASE WHEN (g.pass ->> 'total') ~ '^[0-9]{1,9}$'
         THEN (g.pass ->> 'total')::integer
    END AS findings_digested,
    CASE WHEN (g.pass #>> '{briefing,briefing_id}') ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
         THEN (g.pass #>> '{briefing,briefing_id}')::bigint
    END AS briefing_id,
    COALESCE(g.pass #> '{briefing,body_stored}' = 'true'::jsonb, false)
      AS body_stored
  FROM gathered g
),

-- What the pass did, one count per question a reader of the row asks. Every one of
-- them is a count over the reading above with a predicate, and each predicate is
-- written against the shape its node actually answers rather than against a cast that
-- could raise on something else.

-- findings_selected is the period this digest covered, counted as the ids Select
-- Digest Material answered rather than as the rows the assembly sectioned. The two
-- are the same number today and they answer different questions, this one being about
-- the window and findings_digested about what was laid out inside it.

-- sections_assembled counts the sections the assembly fixed, the uncategorised one
-- among them. It is the only durable record of the taxonomy this digest was laid out
-- under: briefings.payload holds the sections themselves, and nothing joins a stored
-- digest back to the categories that were live when it was written.

-- subscriptions_enabled is how many standing deliveries this domain had at selection
-- time. One is what makes the served_ key below answerable; none and several are what
-- make it absent, and this count is what tells those two apart afterwards.

-- model_calls counts the ledger rows this pass left in llm_calls. The ceiling above
-- admits one, so a number other than nought or one here is that ceiling having moved.
tally AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM reading
      WHERE node = 'findings') AS findings_selected,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM reading
      WHERE node = 'sections') AS sections_assembled,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM reading
      WHERE node = 'subscriptions') AS subscriptions_enabled,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM reading
      WHERE node = 'calls'
        AND (item #>> '{}') ~ '^[0-9]+$') AS model_calls
),

-- The format this pass served, or nothing at all. Two conditions and both are
-- load-bearing: exactly one enabled subscription is what makes the claim answerable,
-- and the pattern is what bounds a value going into a KEY. That member is already
-- CHECK-constrained to five spellings on the table it was read from, so the pattern
-- refuses nothing a subscription row can hold; what it refuses is a member that
-- reached this statement from somewhere else.
served AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN t.subscriptions_enabled = 1
              AND (s.subscription ->> 'format') ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$'
         THEN s.subscription ->> 'format'
    END AS format
  FROM scope s, tally t
),

-- What the pass could not do, one entry per failure, in the shape ar-dispatch's Close
-- Run Failed already writes: the node that met it and the values that say what it
-- was. The ordinal is what keeps two passes failing the same way reporting in the
-- same order.

-- Two entries, and no pass carries both: the first is a briefing row that was not
-- written, the second a row that was written without prose in it.
failure AS (
  SELECT
    1 AS ordinal,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'node', 'Store Briefing',
      'briefing_written', false) AS entry
  FROM scope s
  WHERE s.briefing_id IS NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    2 AS ordinal,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'node', 'Draft Digest Prose',
      'body_stored', false,
      'model_calls', t.model_calls) AS entry
  FROM scope s, tally t
  WHERE s.briefing_id IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT s.body_stored
),

-- The three things the update writes, worked out before it runs so that the statement
-- below is a write and not a decision.

-- The counts are built in two halves and merged. The first half is the fixed set
-- every digest pass reports, put through jsonb_strip_nulls so an unmeasured reading
-- leaves no key rather than a zero. The second is the served_ key, which is one
-- member or none at all, and merging is what lets a key whose NAME is data sit beside
-- keys whose names are written here.
outcome AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN s.briefing_id IS NULL
        THEN 'failed'
      WHEN NOT s.body_stored
        THEN 'partial'
      ELSE 'ok'
    END AS status,
    jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
      'findings_selected', t.findings_selected,
      'findings_digested', s.findings_digested,
      'sections_assembled', t.sections_assembled,
      'subscriptions_enabled', t.subscriptions_enabled,
      'model_calls', t.model_calls,
      'briefings_written', CASE WHEN s.briefing_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END))
    || CASE WHEN v.format IS NOT NULL
            THEN jsonb_build_object('served_' || v.format, 1)
            ELSE '{}'::jsonb
       END AS counts,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT jsonb_agg(f.entry ORDER BY f.ordinal, f.entry) FROM failure f),
      '[]'::jsonb) AS entries
  FROM scope s, tally t, served v
),

-- The write. One row, matched on the run this pass was dispatched with, and nothing
-- else on it is touched: domain_id, started_at and scheduled_by were settled when
-- ar-dispatch opened it, and a closing statement rewriting any of them would be
-- answering a question nobody asked it. scheduled_by in particular stays interval,
-- which runs.scheduled_by records as the mode the DISPATCHER reschedules in rather
-- than a claim about this pass.

-- status and finished_at are set together because nothing in the schema holds them
-- together. A row saying failed with no finish, or carrying a finish while still
-- saying running, is storable, and runs.status records that only the writer pairs
-- them.

-- The entries are APPENDED and not written over. runs.errors defaults to an empty
-- list and this row's id has been outside this workflow since ar-dispatch forwarded
-- it, so a failure recorded against this run by its opener is already there;
-- assigning a fresh list would drop somebody else's account of the same run.

-- No guard against running twice. Closing a run is idempotent in everything but the
-- finish and the appended entries, and nothing on this canvas can produce a second
-- pass, executeOnce leaving exactly one execution and the chain above reaching this
-- node once.
closed AS (
  UPDATE runs r
     SET status = o.status,
         finished_at = now(),
         counts = o.counts,
         errors = r.errors || o.entries
    FROM gathered g, outcome o
   WHERE r.id = g.run_id
  RETURNING r.id
)

SELECT
-- The item this node answers, and the last one this workflow emits. It is what
-- ar-dispatch's Invoke Target Workflow hands to Close Run Succeeded, and the whole
-- reason this node answers exactly one: that branch runs once per item it receives,
-- so a group answering per section would close the dispatcher's row once per section.

-- run_closed is whether the update matched a row. False means the run this pass was
-- dispatched with is no longer there, which is a row deleted mid pass rather than a
-- pass that failed, and the two are worth telling apart in an execution nobody is
-- watching.

-- counts and status travel because they are what this node decided, and reading them
-- back off the answer is cheaper than reading the row again. The briefing itself does
-- not: it is in its own table now, its id is on the item this node was handed, and
-- carrying the digest through the last node of the canvas would put a copy of it on
-- an execution record that has no use for one.
  g.run_id,
  o.status,
  o.counts,
  jsonb_array_length(o.entries) AS errors_appended,
  (SELECT c.id FROM closed c) IS NOT NULL AS run_closed
FROM gathered g, outcome o

[]).map((row) => row.format), findings: ($('Select Digest Material').first().json.findings ?? []).map((row) => row.id), sections: (($('Assemble Digest').first().json.briefing_payload ?? {}).sections ?? []).map((section) => section.key), total: ($('Assemble Digest').first().json.briefing_payload ?? {}).total ?? null, calls: $('Ledger Model Call').all().map((item) => item.json.llm_call_id), briefing: { briefing_id: $('Store Briefing').first().json.briefing_id ?? null, body_stored: $('Store Briefing').first().json.body_stored ?? null } }) }}

parameters.content:
## Dispatched, Never Scheduled

This workflow starts when `ar-dispatch` reaches it through Invoke Target Workflow, and the Execute Workflow Trigger on this canvas is the whole of what makes that possible. It holds no clock and may not acquire one: `ar-dispatch` carries the only Schedule Trigger in the system, and `tests/invariants/workflows.test.ts` counts them across every built workflow and names the one file allowed to hold one.

It is the target of the second of the dispatcher's two claims. A tick reads `topics` and `export_subscriptions` side by side, and `AR_EXPORT_WORKFLOW_ID` in `scripts/workflow-markers.ts` is what pairs a claimed `export` unit with this canvas, the way `AR_TOPIC_WORKFLOW_ID` pairs a claimed topic with `ar-ingest`. So scheduling a digest is a row rather than anything on this canvas: an `export_subscriptions` row carries the interval a digest is produced on and the time it is next due, and changing the cadence is an UPDATE.

### What arrives, and what does not

One item carrying `run_id`, and nothing else. `Open Run` opens the `runs` row before the invocation and its `RETURNING` projection is the item forwarded here, so neither the claimed subscription nor the format it names survives the hop: what this workflow knows about the pass it is running is the run, and the domain is read back off that. `Load Domain Context` is where that happens.

Which subscription the tick claimed is therefore a question about this domain's own `export_subscriptions` rows rather than about the item, and no node here may read the absence as the caller having sent too little. Saying so is the point rather than working around it at the trigger: a member added to that hand-over is a change to `ar-dispatch` and to this canvas together, and a member invented here would be one the dispatcher never sent.

The trigger is typeVersion 1, which passes the caller's item through as it stands. Nothing here declares an input schema, so what the dispatcher sends is what the first node reads, and adding a schema later is a change to both ends rather than to this node alone.

### Nothing here sends

No workflow in this set holds a send-capable node, and this is the canvas where that rule is easiest to doubt: a digest is the thing a subscriber would be sent. What a pass here does instead is store. A `briefings` row is where a period's digest lives, which is what makes every format render the same text rather than compose its own, and turning one into an artifact belongs to a renderer under `src/exports/`, which returns bytes to a caller and delivers nothing either. `docs/architecture/01-invariants.md` carries both halves of that rule and names the test that fails when either stops holding.

### Started by hand

A run started from this canvas rather than by the dispatcher carries no `run_id`, and nothing pretends otherwise. `Load Domain Context` answers a null `run_id`, a null `domain_id`, a null domain row and four empty lists, which is a shape a node below can refuse by name. It is not an error worth suppressing: a pass with no run to charge has nowhere to write what it did, and a pass with no domain has no findings to digest and no subscription to have been dispatched for.

nodes.name: The Boundary Is What Was Stored

parameters.content:
## The Boundary Is What Was Stored

What one digest covers is decided in this group, and the deciding value is a row rather than a clock. `Select Digest Material` reads the `generated_at` stamp on the newest `briefings` row this domain has and selects the findings created at or after it. Nothing in the statement reads `now()`, so two passes an hour apart over a domain nothing has written to select the same findings.

That is what makes a period a fact about what was last stored rather than about how often the dispatcher happens to fire. A subscription whose cadence an operator doubles produces twice as many digests covering half as much each, and one switched off for a month and back on produces a single digest covering the month. Neither needs a span written down anywhere, and neither can leave a gap between two periods: every finding created after the last stamp is in the next digest, whenever that pass runs.

`briefings` carries no column naming the period a row covers, which its own TSDoc in `src/db/schema/runs.ts` records as the trade it makes. So the boundary is the stamp on the row before, and what a stored briefing covered is readable as the span between its stamp and its predecessor's rather than out of any column.

### A domain with nothing stored gets its whole corpus, once

The first pass over a domain that has never had a digest has no stamp to bound anything with, so it selects every finding the domain holds. That is the intent rather than a fallback, and it happens exactly once: the pass writes a `briefings` row, and the pass after it starts from that row's stamp.

There is no row cap on the selection, and its absence is what makes the once hold. A cap would drop the tail of a long corpus, and the next window starts at this briefing's stamp, so what it dropped would never come round again. An unbounded first pass over a large corpus is the cost, paid once per domain. What a pass may SPEND on the model call is bounded in that group, over what it drafts, which bounds a cost rather than what the period covered.

### The one thing a stamp cannot bound

A pass selects at one moment and its briefing is stamped at a later one, so a finding written between the two is outside this digest and outside the next one, whose window starts at that stamp. Closing it needs the selection's own high water mark stored on the briefing, which is a column that table does not have. The bound is inclusive at the other end for the same reason: a finding created at exactly the stamp is carried rather than dropped, and it duplicates nothing, the previous pass having selected before its own write.

### Which subscription came due is not answerable here

`Load Domain Context` above leaves that question to this group, and the answer is that the claimed row does not survive the hop: `Open Run` in `ar-dispatch` ends `RETURNING id AS run_id`. So this node reads every ENABLED `export_subscriptions` row the domain holds, which is the set the claim was taken from. A domain holding exactly one is answered exactly and `subscription` IS that row; a domain holding several is answered with all of them and a NULL where the one row would go, rather than with a choice this statement invented.

Nothing is lost by that, because what a pass produces does not depend on which subscription it was dispatched for. The `briefings` row is the same row whichever one came due, storing the digest being what makes every format render the same text, and a format selects a renderer rather than changing what a period came to. Where the exact row is wanted the repair is a wider `RETURNING` in `ar-dispatch` and a member read here, the two together.

### The run before this one

The `errors` of the newest CLOSED `runs` row for this domain travel with the selection, so a period whose preceding pass failed says so in the digest rather than only in a table nobody reading a digest opens. `previousRunBanner` in `src/lib/digest-assemble.ts` is what makes a banner of them. It is whichever workflow opened that row: `runs` names no writer, so the newest closed one may be an ingest, a capture, a score or a research pass, and what a digest reports is that the domain's last pass failed at something rather than which canvas it was.

## Stored Rather Than Sent

`Store Briefing` writes one `briefings` row, and that row is the whole of what this canvas produces about the period. The node after it closes the run the dispatcher opened, which is the pass's account of itself rather than anything a reader of a digest is shown. The prose the drafting call came back with goes in `body`, the structure `Assemble Digest` fixed goes in `payload`, and nothing else about the pass leaves the database.

Storing it is what makes every format render the same text. `briefings` in `src/db/schema/runs.ts` argues it from the schema side and `src/exports/index.ts` argues it again from the renderer side: an export and the API serve one artifact rather than two renderings able to disagree about what a period came to. A renderer handed the findings and asked to compose prose out of them would be exactly that second rendering, and nothing afterwards would say which of the two the domain had meant. All four renderers read this row back and none of them writes one.

### Where the send-free rule leaves a digest pass able to finish

`docs/architecture/00-overview.md` states the rule: the workflows write to the database, renderers return artifacts, and an email export produces a draft and stops there. A digest pass therefore cannot end in a delivery, and with no row written it would end in nothing at all -- a selection, an assembly and one model call, spent and then dropped. This node is the ending the rule leaves open, which is why it is where the pass's whole output lands rather than one step among several. What it is not yet is the ending for a pass that staged nothing: `Apply Call Ceiling` ends the chain above this node for a period that came to nothing and for a pass that resolved no domain, so neither writes a row, and closing that needs a path around the model group rather than a flag on it.

### No artifact is written anywhere by this canvas

Nothing here opens a file, reaches a vault, addresses a recipient or resolves a destination. The `export_subscriptions` rows `Select Digest Material` read name a FORMAT and a connector, and neither is a place this statement writes to: which subscription came due decides which renderer the stored digest is later put through and changes nothing about the row. Rendering happens outside this workflow, in a module under `src/exports/` that `tests/invariants/exports-send-free.test.ts` holds to a transport-free rule of its own, over the row written here. Delivery is a later capability behind its own approval gate and exists nowhere in this set today.

### A NULL body is not an empty one

The drafting step can come back with nothing, in three shapes: a call that failed and was let through by `onError: continueRegularOutput`, an answer carrying no text member at all, and text whose whole content is blank. All three store SQL NULL rather than `''`. The column states the difference and this node is what holds to it -- NULL means no text was produced, where `''` would claim a briefing was written and that it came to nothing, which a surface then renders as a blank document rather than as nothing to show. `composeMarkdownBody` in `src/exports/markdown-body.ts` is what acts on the split, composing a digest out of its structure alone.

The trim is the emptiness test rather than the value. Whatever survives it is stored as the model wrote it, untrimmed and unreduced, and every renderer puts the stored body through `sanitizeUntrusted` on its own way out. That is where the reduction belongs: a Postgres node splices no library, and reducing on the way in would leave nobody able to compare what is stored against what the model actually said. The assembled half beside it needs none, `Assemble Digest` having reduced text that came out of this domain's own tables before it assembled anything.

### The row this pass writes is the next pass's boundary

`briefings` carries no unique key over a period, so this is an insert with no conflict target: a second render of the same domain adds a rival row rather than meeting the first, and the current digest is the newest by `generated_at`. That stamp dates the write, and `Select Digest Material` bounds the next window by the newest stored one, so what lands here is where the following period starts.

nodes.name: A Row It Did Not Open

parameters.content:
## A Row It Did Not Open

`Close Digest Run` finishes the `runs` row `ar-dispatch` opened before it invoked this workflow. Every other node on this canvas writes about the period; this one writes about the pass, in the three columns `runs` keeps that account in -- `status` is what the pass came to, `counts` is what it did, `errors` is what it could not do.

Nothing here opened that row, which is what makes this node an `UPDATE` where `ar-score` and `ar-capture` both `INSERT`. Those two are invoked and open nothing; this workflow and `ar-ingest` are dispatched, and a dispatched pass arrives holding a run id and no row of its own to write.

### The dispatcher waits on it, and then writes the row again

`Invoke Target Workflow` in `ar-dispatch` sets `waitForSubWorkflow`, so the tick that dispatched this pass is still open while every node above runs, and `Close Run Succeeded` fires on the item this node answers. That statement sets `status` and `finished_at` itself, landing an `ok` on top of whatever was written here. What survives either way is `counts`, which no statement in `ar-dispatch` touches, and `errors`, which both sides append to rather than assign. So the status written here is the pass's own reading of itself and the row's last word on it belongs to whichever writer wrote last -- the open choice `Close Run Succeeded` names, between reading `errors` on that side and holding every target to reporting its own status.

Answering exactly one item is what keeps that second write singular. `Close Run Succeeded` runs once per item this workflow returns, so a canvas answering three would close the dispatcher's row three times. `executeOnce` is set here and the node above already answers one item.

### Which subscription a pass served, recorded as a count

`counts` is a map of counts, which `runs.counts` in `src/db/schema/runs.ts` annotates and `ar-score`'s own closing node refused to break for a feature version. So the format is written as a KEY rather than as a value: `served_obsidian_md` at 1 says which renderer the stored digest was dispatched for, and every value in the column is still a count.

It is written only where the claim is answerable. `Open Run` in `ar-dispatch` returns the run id alone, so which subscription came due does not survive the hop, and `Select Digest Material` answers a fail-closed identity in its place: the row where the domain has exactly one enabled subscription, and nothing where it has none or several. `subscriptions_enabled` beside it tells those two apart afterwards. Neither is a failure -- a domain wanting one digest in two formats is ordinary, and `briefings` argues why it costs nothing, a pass writing the SAME row whichever subscription came due.

### An unmeasured count is absent rather than nought

`counts` cannot hold a null, so the null-vs-zero rule is kept here by leaving the key out. `jsonb_strip_nulls` drops a reading that was not a number, and a reader finds no key rather than a nought claiming something was measured at nothing.

### What each status means for a digest

`partial` is a briefing stored with no prose in it: the structure `Assemble Digest` fixed is in the row and the drafting call came back with nothing, which is the split `RUN_STATUSES` keeps the member for. `failed` is no row written at all, which no path here reaches, `Store Briefing`'s insert being unconditional -- it is read fail-closed anyway. `ok` is both halves stored.

The run a pass never reaches is unchanged by this group. A period that came to nothing stops at `Apply Call Ceiling`, so its row keeps the `running` default and `ar-dispatch` cannot finish it either, its success branch having no item to fire on. The repair is a path around the model group and belongs to the canvas rather than to this node.
